newsitem.title: ITALY: World banana surplus seen by 1999 - FAO.
newsitem.headline: World banana surplus seen by 1999 - FAO.

text.p: The United Nations Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO) forecast on Wednesday that banana supply would outstrip demand by 1999, leading to unsustainable world surpluses of the tropical fruit.

"World import demands for bananas is projected to grow by about 3.6 percent annually, from 10.6 million tonnes in 1995 to 12.2 million tonnes in 1999," FAO said in a report to be presented to a three-day intergovernmental conference in Rome which opens on Wednesday.
"World export availabilities between 1995-99 are expected to grow by three percent per year, to reach nearly 12.9 million tonnes," the report said.
FAO forecast that by 1999 there would be an oversupply of 650,000 tonnes of the fruit with little chance of an upturn in demand in the import markets of Europe and the United States.
"Such large surpluses are not sustainable," the report said.
"Indeed, the global banana industry already appears to be making some required adjustments whereby reductions in surpluses could be expected."
The agency added that lower world prices, pushed down by oversupply, have already dampened incentives to expand production in Latin America, the world's largest banana exporter.
